**Phase:** PLANNING. **Goal:** Replace the factory electrical system: PMU-24 DL, rear lithium battery, four modular harness legs, every switch a ladder, and both custom modules - the ICU and the DCU, with their firmware; the car drives on it before anything else joins

**Yours:** 11 you can do now, 15 waiting. **Agent:** 2 ready, 16 blocked.

The car stays whole through Part 1. It comes apart once, at **S1**, which waits on everything in Part 1; Part 2 is everything that needs it apart, then the design review and your freeze. [The build list](../01-build/TODO.md) picks up from the car apart and ends with it back together.

  The PMU is already bought (00-CAR vehicle). 12 V bench supply, meter in series, let it sleep, read mA. LD17 assumes 150 mA; at that the 40 Ah pack reaches its BMS cut-off in about 11 days, with no slow-crank warning (SP-232). Same bench session as F-009, Q-028 and Q-110

- [ ] **V-002** — Alternator output rating  
  read the rating off the alternator tag -- The case reads only "B" / Mitsubishi. The 1980 and 1985 workshop manuals both give a 55 A Mitsubishi unit (`00-CAR/SPECS.md` SP-078, SP-079 — the 1985 part is A5T30574; the 1981–83 fiche lists N221-18-300R, SP-006); an enthusiast chart says 50 A for base cars (SP-080, unverified). Read the rating stamped on the case to settle which the 1982 GS automatic carries. Nothing in the harness depends on it — F18 is 100 A and the 6 AWG B+ cable carries 100 A — but the charging figures at install 2.14 cannot be called good or bad without it. It also feeds the D-179 no-charge diagnosis: D-198 rebuilt the excitation circuit, and this is the number that says whether a healthy unit is behaving.
- [ ] **W-330b** — Ask Ionic for the BLE protocol map for the IC-12V40-S9H, and for the S9H heater's own figures  
  Ask for the frame map on FFE0/FFE1: message types beyond 0x01, the command set for requesting current and state of charge, and the scale factors. Say the pack is an IC-12V40-S9H and that the type-01 cell frame already decodes at ~1.43 mV/count. This is what turns D-330 from voltage-only into the full picture without a shunt. **Second ask, added 2026-09-12 (V-052):** at what temperature the S9H's heater turns on and off, how much it draws, and whether it can draw from the pack itself or only from an active charging source. Self-heating packs of this class only heat while charging, which would take the heater off the sleeping budget entirely - but Ionic publishes nothing for the S9H, so it is unverified (00-CAR SP-233). One email, two answers. **Third ask, added 2026-09-23 (risk review, D-386):** below about 0 C a LiFePO4 must not take charge - does the S9H's BMS then only refuse charge current, or does it disconnect the pack from the car altogether? If it disconnects while the engine runs, the alternator is suddenly unloaded (a load dump the P136 TVS exists for) and the car runs with no battery behind it.

## Part 2 · Interior out — strip the interior - leave every wire in place, then everything that needs the car apart

### Your checklist

  *waits on:* 26 earlier rows - everything above this one  
  The first step with the car apart; it waits on every design step that can be done with the car whole, so the car is off the road as short a time as possible. Out: seats, console, centre stack, dash and cluster (unplugged, not cut), glovebox, carpet, kick and sill panels, cargo-bin trim. Nothing electrical is cut, unpinned or moved - every factory wire stays connected where it is. Bag and label every fastener by panel, and photograph every connector and loom run where it lies before anything is disturbed (that is M-7). The clear width, height and depth of the centre-stack cavity, the glovebox region and the floor under the dash on both sides; lever clearance; 60 mm behind the receptacles. Two riders now: where the wideband gauge hides, and whether its fixed sensor lead reaches the bung from there (D-244).
- ⏳ **Q-110** — How long does the horn take from asleep?  
  *waits on:* C1 (yours: M-1 dash envelope, plus where the wideband gauge hides and whether …)  
  waits also on E25 (the PMU configured). a stopwatch measurement on a sleeping car -- Horn, hazard, wink — and now the brake (D-247 → D-278) — all work with the key out, and all of them work by *waking the module first*: the stage lifts pin 7, the PMU boots, decodes and drives the output. Nothing in the design says how long that takes, and the horn is the one control whose whole value is in its first 200 milliseconds. Measure it at §5.4 with a stopwatch and a helper: press the pad on a sleeping car, time until it sounds. Under ~200 ms, say nothing more about it. Over ~500 ms, decide whether the horn should hang off the always-hot busbar through its own relay instead — a change this build can still absorb and a finished car cannot. The brake is the same measurement and matters more.
- ⏳ **Q-115** — Road speed: the car may already have a signal, at the dash  
  *waits on:* C1 (yours: M-1 dash envelope, plus where the wideband gauge hides and whether …)  
  waits also on install M-6. a check at the speedometer head with the cluster out -- The speedometer is cable-driven and there is no electronic speed signal in the design - a digital cluster needs one. But the 1982 component list carries a **vehicle speed switch (B-29)**: a reed switch **inside the speedometer head** that pulses to ground on a single `BR` wire. It fed cruise control, which D-097 deleted, so it is sitting there unused and **terminating behind the dash**. **Check at M-6**, with the cluster out anyway: find the `BR` wire at the speedometer head, confirm it pulses to ground as the cable turns, and count pulses per wheel revolution. If it checks out, road speed costs **one conductor** into a free `L3-S2 12` or `L3-S3` cavity and the tunnel run is deleted from the plan. If it does not, the fallback is an inline pass-through sensor at the transmission (3-wire Hall, 12 V square wave, keeps the mechanical sp

- ⏳ **V-081** — Pop-up drive conductors  
  *waits on:* C1 (yours: M-1 dash envelope, plus where the wideband gauge hides and whether …)  
  waits also on teardown. a look at the pop-up motor conductors -- install M-3. **Sharpened by T-017, 2026-09-12: the connector is a FOUR-way, not two conductors.** The section E scan shows E-03 / E-04 with WR, YG, R and RY, the factory feeding the motor on WR and commanding it on R / RY, while the design caps WR and drives R / RY. Ohming only R and RY to case cannot tell those topologies apart, so the check is now CK08: every pair and every terminal to case, at parked, half-raised and raised, on each motor. This is the one measurement the pin plan waits on (D-186, D-199) - five minutes, before the L2 leg is pinned.
